reachable: Yes, at the scored position and in training. to_obs is applied unconditionally to the read-position prediction in every scoring path (evolve/cups_probe.py:275, 405, 609; eval/adapter.py:204; evolve/cdh_probe.py:165, 238) with no dependence on an observation being present, so the mechanism is live at the read -- unlike the observation-gated failure this search has already seen. The module holds zero trainable parameters (all state is buffers), so "does it get gradient" does not apply; it acts by reshaping the metric of the main loss at every command position of every batch, which I confirmed live: transformed-target rms drops 1.000 -> 0.232 at step 150 and the loss visibly changes trajectory. The maps also survive into scoring correctly -- eval/adapter.py:197-198 deepcopies net.target_module (registered buffers, so fwd_map/inv_map come along) and _linear_map moves the matrix to the prediction's device/dtype per call. Buffers cannot update at scoring time: _observe is only called from make_target, which no scoring path calls, and is additionally guarded by self.training and torch.is_grad_enabled(). One caveat: the mechanism is identity for the first 149 of the ~4000 steps, so ~96% of training runs whitened.
solves_outside_model: No. The target impl parses no command text; its only input is z_obs, and its only state is one global 768x768 second moment aggregated over the entire training stream. It cannot represent, and never sees, a per-window routing fact. Both scoring arms are mapped by the same frozen matrix, so a predictor keyed on the location being read still cancels to exactly zero -- the differential's cancellation property is untouched. The two impls in this genome that DO parse command strings are both the legitimate kind: r2_routedepth_tilt_readcollision_blocks walks the mv graph out of `cmds` but returns only a list of integer indices (harness.py:81 bounds-checks it) and never mutates a sequence dict or a token -- pure sample selection; it also uses z_obs at the read position for its near-duplicate-answer masking, which shapes WHICH sequences are batched together, not what the model reads. r3_srcdst_hashslot_coding is the parent's stream and is covered by the read-token invariant the instrument enforces (evolve/cups_probe.py, the code_cmds arm-difference check). Nothing resolved in Python reaches the model as input at scoring time.
summary: The candidate is what it says it is at the level that matters for the archive: a global, output-side, chain-agnostic ZCA reparameterisation of the target space, exactly invertible, applied to the training target and undone at readout, carrying no routing information and live at the scored read. Its most unusual claims -- the jail data statistics -- reproduce exactly, including the two-distinct-empty-strings fact, and the exact-inverse, symmetric-branch, shrinkage, warmup-identity, training-mode-only and one-global-matrix claims all hold under execution. The crossover rationale is also accurate: the batcher, arch, head-parameter and optim descriptions each match their code. Two quantitative claims are wrong in a way a later reader would inherit. First, the c rescale normalises against the shrunk second moment, not the real one, so "fixes the average per-dimension variance at 1" -- the stated reason r12's absolute constants stay in regime -- held to 0.054 rather than 1 in a full end-to-end run on the standard fixture, and my spectrum sweep shows the claim degrades from 0.91 to 0.08 as effective rank falls from ~30 to ~10. Whether real standardized observation embeddings land in the safe regime is the one thing I could not check, and it is the same unknown the author flagged as failure mode 1. Second, the stated amplification cap of 3.05 omits the c factor; the true bound is 1/sqrt(shrink) = 4.47, and I measured ||W||_2 = 4.37, above the 4.0 spectral cap the author's own risk analysis relies on. Finally, everything labelled "MEASURED IN THE JAIL" could not have been executed (no torch there); I reproduced the timings and round-trip errors independently and they hold, so this is a false provenance label rather than invented data.

divergences.claim: "the rescale by c, which fixes the average per-dimension variance of the transformed target at 1, so the objective's absolute constants (r12's _DELTA, _MARGIN, the precision clamps) stay in the regime they were tuned in."
divergences.what_the_code_does: c is computed from the SHRUNK matrix S = 0.95*M + 0.05*I (trace_after = sum lam_i^(1-p) over eigenvalues of S), but the target it rescales is drawn from the UNSHRUNK second moment M. The identity trace(W M W^T)/D = 1 holds only when M ~= S. Whenever M has directions well below the 0.05 shrink floor -- exactly the rank-poor regime the shrinkage is advertised to protect against -- the transformed target's average per-dimension variance falls far below 1, without bound on the low side.
divergences.evidence: Ran the full genome through the real training closure on eval/guard_reach's fixture (200 steps, cpu): raw target rms 1.000 at every step, transformed target rms 0.232 from step 150 on -> mean per-dim variance 0.054, an 18x deviation from the claimed 1. The main loss also stepped UP when the map switched on (6.190 at step 149 -> 6.716 at step 150) and had not returned to its pre-switch level by step 200. Analytic sweep over spectra with trace fixed at D=768 (t4.py): isotropic 1.000; power law i^-1 (eff rank 32) 0.911; i^-1.5 (eff rank 5.4) 0.602; i^-2 0.266; rank-100-flat + near-null floor 0.358; rank-10 0.081. So the claim is accurate to ~10% for effective rank >= ~30 and wrong by 3-18x below that. Consequence is exactly what the sentence promises to prevent: r12's _DELTA=0.05 duplicate cutoff and _MARGIN=0.5 repulsion hinge are absolute in per-dimension squared-distance units (evolve/chunks/objective/r12_antiretrieval_ring_negatives.py:23,26,51,55-59,82), so a 0.054 target variance puts typical target-target distances at ~0.11 and saturates the hinge. I could NOT determine which regime the real standardized obs embeddings fall in -- the fixture is deliberately degenerate (3 boards, ~10 distinct observation directions), and the author's own quoted synthetic spectrum (242/0.28) computes to 0.95 under my sweep, i.e. fine.

divergences.claim: "The SHRINKAGE toward I bounds how much any direction can be amplified (at p=0.75 the cap is (1/0.05)^0.375 = 3.05)", and in failure mode 2, "whose spectral cap of 4.0 comfortably contains ||W||_2 = 3.37 as measured on the synthetic frame".
divergences.what_the_code_does: 3.05 is max S^(-p/2) BEFORE the c rescale that the code then applies (f = f * scale, line 69). The realised cap is c * shrink^(-p/2), and c is itself bounded by shrink^(-(1-p)/2) = 1.454, so the true worst case is shrink^(-1/2) = 4.472 -- independent of p. The stated bound understates the code by up to 1.454x.
divergences.evidence: Measured ||W||_2 = 4.370 in the end-to-end run at step 150 and 4.387 at step 200 (t3.py) -- 43% above the stated 3.05 and above the 4.0 spectral cap the author's failure-mode-2 argument relies on (spectral_cap=4.0 confirmed at evolve/chunks/optim/r18_spectral_capped_transition_readout.py:66,155). Spectrum sweep reaches 4.33 for a rank-10 frame, against the analytic bound 4.472. The claim is not merely a loose bound: it is the number the hypothesis uses to argue the net can compensate W through a capped (D,D) readout, and that argument does not survive the correction.

divergences.claim: "Neither program touches the target space: both train on the raw standardized observation embedding under identity. Their loss therefore weights every direction of the target distribution by that distribution's own spread."
divergences.what_the_code_does: The first sentence is true (target = identity in both parents). The second overstates the baseline: r12 already applies a bounded per-dimension inverse-precision weight w = (1/(mse_d+1e-2))^0.5, mean-normalised and clamped to [0.25, 4.0], to the contrastive distances.
divergences.evidence: evolve/chunks/objective/r12_antiretrieval_ring_negatives.py:38-46. The novel content of this candidate survives the correction -- w is diagonal (axis-aligned) and keyed on the model's own residual, while W is a full rotation keyed on the target spread, so the ZCA does something the existing term structurally cannot -- but the stated baseline is not what the code does, and a reader taking the hypothesis at face value would credit the candidate with introducing per-direction reweighting that partly already existed.

divergences.claim: "COST, MEASURED IN THE JAIL, NOT EXTRAPOLATED": mean 4.4 ms/step over 400 steps, worst step 45 ms, 5.1 s total; roundtrip "measured 1.5e-5 absolute / 7e-7 relative on a 768-d synthetic target set"; "||W||_2 = 3.37 as measured on the synthetic frame"; "Full stack ... 20 and 80 steps runs finite and decreasing, stream.leakage_ok passes".
divergences.what_the_code_does: Per verified ground truth the inventor had no torch in the jail, so none of these could have been executed as stated. The values are nevertheless essentially right when I run them.
divergences.evidence: Reproduced independently: 400 steps at n=2000 took 6.72 s wall including batch synthesis, worst single make_target 45.9 ms (the float64 eigh) -- claimed 45 ms; round trip 3.6e-5 absolute / 7.0e-7 relative on my synthetic (claimed 1.5e-5 / 7e-7; the absolute figure is scale-dependent, the relative one matches); full stack finite and decreasing over 200 real steps. The internal arithmetic is also self-consistent (gains 0.145 / 1.92 reproduce c * S^(-0.375) on their quoted spectrum, and 0.145^2 = 1/47.6 matches their "loses ~47x of its weight"). So this is a false provenance label on numbers that hold, not fabricated numbers -- but the hypothesis presents unexecuted results as measured, and the archive would record them that way.

divergences.claim: "One parameter change for coherence: head params pred_weight 0.0 ... Zeroing it removes the only space-conflicting term and leaves the head's mechanism ... intact."
divergences.what_the_code_does: True of the loss terms: pred_weight gates exactly the third aux term (the InfoNCE on the arch's own prediction) and nothing else, and the transport memory still reaches the prediction through the zero-init out_scale in the wrapped forward. But a space conflict remains on the FORWARD path: read_weight/mse_weight pin reads_t to raw observation space, and reads_t is injected into a prediction that must now live in W-space through rgate * out_scale, a scalar gate times a DIAGONAL vector, which cannot rotate. This is the same defect the author does acknowledge for the arch's direct injection in failure mode 2, but it is not acknowledged for the head.
divergences.evidence: evolve/chunks/head/r2_dualaddress_move_transport.py:100 (out_scale is a per-dimension nn.Parameter), 149 (contrib = rgate * reads_t * out_scale), 177-179 (added into cmd-position predictions), 301-305 (only the pred_weight term is gated off). Confirmed head_p = {'pred_weight': 0.0} is the only head param override in genome.json.

divergences.claim: "identity for the first 150 steps" / "exactly 0 before the first refresh".
divergences.what_the_code_does: _observe runs before _linear_map inside make_target, so the rebuild at the 150th observation is applied to that same step's target. Identity holds for steps 1-149.
divergences.evidence: t1.py: |fwd_map - I| max = 0.000e+00 at steps 1, 149 and 1.793e-01 at step 150. Off by one; no consequence.
